summary: Every clip above 300k views in this campaign uses a single on-screen text block that is fully visible from frame one and never changes across all three shots — the entire joke is absorbed in under two seconds. The winning premise is a relatable, community-legible meme written in casual internet vernacular (sentence case, white text, 1-2 emojis at the tail end) built on a sharp contrast or absurd specificity: Lucia doing something endearing that contradicts her criminal identity, Jason & Lucia couple dynamics, platform-envy pain, or fan-loyalty sacrifice. Rank 1 (2.9M) proves that a universally known real-life meme format ('fake shower method') transplanted onto Lucia is the single highest-ceiling move in this campaign — the joke requires zero GTA lore, only recognition of Lucia as a charac

title_formula: Lead with the meme premise in 6-10 words exactly as someone would type it in a comment — conversational, no forced grammar. Drop one emotional emoji immediately after. Close with #GTA6. Do NOT start with 'When' or 'POV' — that pattern is overused. Examples: 'Lucia discovering the fake shower method
caption_formula: One sentence that restates the meme idea in different wording from the on-screen text — never copy it verbatim, max 20 words. Line break. Then '🎵 Tokyo Girl — Passive' on its own line for song credit (campaign rule). Line break. Then hashtags on a final line. Example: 'She is literally a wanted crim
avoid: Changing the on-screen text between shots — ranks 1, 2, 3, 5, and 7 all hold one static block across every beat; no evidence the 3-beat escalating structure outperforms this yet, so static remains def
ALL CAPS text — every high-performing campaign clip uses sentence case; caps reads aggressive, not funny, in this meme register
Premises that require deep GTA lore — the two highest clips (2.9M, 1M) are legible to anyone who has seen Lucia's face once; lore-heavy jokes narrow the audience before the hook can land
Soft or low-contrast setups with no absurdist spike — warmth without contradiction consistently underperforms in this campaign
More than 2 emojis inside the on-screen text block — top clips use exactly 1-2 at the very end only; front-loaded emojis do not appear in any top performer
Voiceover, dialogue, or any audio other than Tokyo Girl — campaign rule, zero exceptions
